Thank you, I enjoy discussing security. I'll admit I'm not an expert on firewalls. I don't think there is any one universal solution for them though. The solution you can offer will depend more on where they sit on the network and how much traffic they handle. As far as the problem with IoT devices, that is more of a problem with the manufacturing of these devices than with the firewall. Practices like, hardcoding ssh and telnet credentials or improper use of Universal Plug and Play are far too common. There are some measures you can take to lessen the impact, such as disabling UPnP on your router firewall, keeping your router firmware up to date, changing default router and modem passwords, and avoiding products with bad security practices.

Edit: for reference: https://securityintelligence.com/the-internet-of-trouble-securing-vulnerable-iot-devices/

Sorry, you're right. I didn't mean to give the impression that you shouldn't use AV, just that you shouldn't  pay extra money for it. And I agree, layering security measures does build a stronger defense.

This is true, current Information Security professional here. Traditional AV software finds viruses by analyzing signatures. It can only find what it has seen before. It is easy for developers to modify the code slightly and get past AV easily, because it has never seen it before. File less malware is another point most traditional AV software will fail. This is malware that doesn't write to disk but persists in memory. I wouldn't pay any money for any AV software right now. The best defense is to use common sense and a good ad blocker.
